body.title: A native element of your node
body.description: Native elements come with the core at the first start and serve the core and every other element. This is the template each of them is built from.

body.text: The installer puts every native element in place by its pinned tag at the first start.
The core and the custom elements call its doors; it has no working process and takes no payments.
Native elements open the stores with the node’s data key, each finding named by its element.
The core does not delete a native element or move its address; its code is open and yours to change.
Native elements are never sold and never join an outside network.

body.title: On by default, except Stripe and Redis

body.text: Every native element arrives turned on, except Stripe, which waits for its keys, and the fast store (Redis), which waits for an application that needs it. The node holds the switch of each.

body.title: Your own builder comes with it

body.text: Every element of the node comes with its own Claude Code agent and can get its own Telegram bot. When something in this element should change, write to its bot from your phone, and the agent updates the logic or the design.
The agent works only in its element's folder and never reads the whole node, so each change costs fewer tokens. Your Claude Code subscription pays for it.

items: The element's bot is connected in the core, on its «Telegram» page.
The agent returns a commit; you look at it in «Preview» and accept it or turn it down.
At the computer, the agent's terminal is in the core, in this element's «Build».

body.text: Built by Fractera for the [Lagrix](https://lagrix.dev) protocol. MIT license, the template is at [github.com/Fractera/fractera-native-item-starter](https://github.com/Fractera/fractera-native-item-starter).

items.a: An element that comes with the core at the first start and serves the core and the other elements: sign-in, data, the stores, settings, payments.

items.q: Can a native element be removed?
items.a: Sign-in, data and root can be replaced but not deleted.

items.q: Does a native element sell work to others?
items.a: No. A native element has no working process and no payments of its own.
